newsitem.title: NORWAY: Storebrand sees competition staying tough.
newsitem.headline: Storebrand sees competition staying tough.

text.p: Competition in the Norwegian insurance market is expected to remain tough but some of the more aggressive policies on prices may let up, according to the head of Norway's largest insurance group Storebrand ASA.

"The competition is fierce, it has been for a long time and it will continue to be fierce. I don't particularly foresee any shift in competition," Storebrand Chief Executive Aage Korsvold said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
Kosvold was speaking after the company released nine-month group profits at 922 million crowns, down 28 percent from the corresponding year-ago period.
Storebrand attributed the decline to unusually high losses in the non-life sector in the third quarter and a 250 million crown provision for restructuring the organisation.
"I don't expect prices to pick up, but I expect maybe that some of the most aggressive pricing practices will abate somewhat," Kosvold told RFTV.
"We can see from other published results that this very aggressive pricing posture is taking its toll on results."
